intent_en: To illustrate the significant and widening partisan divide in COVID-19 vaccination rates, demonstrating that Democrats are much more likely than Republicans to have received a vaccine.
previous_intent: To illustrate the persistent and significant partisan divide in COVID-19 vaccination rates, showing that Democrats are much more likely to have received the vaccine than Republicans throughout the early months of 2021.
narration_support: We find that Democrats are significantly more likely than Republicans to say they've received a vaccine for COVID -19, and this gap is as big or wider than at any point during the course of the outbreak.
chart_support: Line chart tracking the percentage of U.S. adults who received a COVID-19 vaccine from Feb 2021 to Aug 2021, showing a steep increase for Democrats compared to Republicans and a widening gap between the two groups over time.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly states the gap is wide and Democrats are more likely to be vaccinated. The chart visualizes this with two lines (Dem/Rep) diverging significantly from Feb '21 to Aug '21, with the Dem line ending much higher.
